questions.question: In which of the following years will India host the World Badminton Championship?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years will India host the World Badminton Championship?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2026.

Key Points

  • India has been selected to host the BWF World Championships in 2026.
  • This prestigious event is one of the most significant tournaments in the badminton world, drawing top players from across the globe.
  • The decision to award India the hosting rights reflects the country's growing prominence in the sport of badminton.
  • India has previously hosted the BWF World Championships in 2009, showcasing its capability to manage such large-scale international events.

Additional Information

  • BWF World Championships
    • The Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Championships is the most prestigious tournament in the sport of badminton.
    • It was first held in 1977 and is now conducted annually, except in Olympic years.
    • The tournament determines the world champions in five disciplines: men’s singles, women’s singles, men’s doubles, women’s doubles, and mixed doubles.
    • Winning a title at the BWF World Championships is considered a significant achievement and highly coveted among badminton players.
  • Badminton in India
    • Badminton is one of the most popular sports in India, with a growing number of players achieving international success.
    • India has produced several world-class badminton players such as Prakash Padukone, Pullela Gopichand, Saina Nehwal, and PV Sindhu.
    • PV Sindhu made history by becoming the first Indian woman to win a silver medal in badminton at the 2016 Rio Olympics.
    • The Badminton Association of India (BAI) is the governing body responsible for the development and promotion of badminton in the country.
  • Significance of Hosting International Sports Events
    • Hosting international sports events like the BWF World Championships can have significant benefits for the host country.It helps in boosting tourism and the local economy, generating global visibility, and enhancing the country’s reputation as a capable and reliable event organizer.

questions.question: When was pro kabaddi league inaugurated for the first time in India?

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • The Pro Kabaddi League was inaugurated for the first time in India in 2014.
  • It was established with the aim to popularize the sport of kabaddi and provide a professional platform for players.
  • The league was inspired by the success of the kabaddi tournament at the 2006 Asian Games.
  • The inaugural season of the Pro Kabaddi League featured eight teams, which competed in a double round-robin format followed by playoffs.

Additional Information

  • Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)
    • The Pro Kabaddi League is a professional-level kabaddi league in India, established in 2014.
    • It is organized by Mashal Sports and STAR India, with the backing of the Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI), the Asian Kabaddi Federation (AKF), and the International Kabaddi Federation (IKF).
    • The league follows a format similar to that of the Indian Premier League (IPL), with franchises representing various cities across India.
    • Players from different countries, including Iran, South Korea, and Kenya, participate in the league, making it a global event.
    • The league has significantly contributed to the growth and popularity of kabaddi, both in India and internationally.
  • Kabaddi
    • Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in ancient India.
    • The game involves two teams of seven players each, who take turns sending a "raider" into the opposing team's half of the court to tag as many defenders as possible and return to their half of the court without being tackled.
    • Points are scored by the raider for each defender tagged, while the opposing team earns points for stopping the raider.
    • Kabaddi is known for its fast-paced and physically demanding nature, requiring strength, agility, and strategic thinking.

    • The 1924 Summer Olympics, officially known as the Games of the VIII Olympiad, were held in Paris, France.

    • India first participated in the Olympics in 1900, when Norman Pritchard represented the country and won two silver medals in athletics.
    • After the 1924 Paris Olympics, India has consistently participated in every Summer Olympic Games.
    • India's first gold medal was won by the men's field hockey team in the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics.
    • Over the years, India has earned numerous medals in various sports, with significant achievements in field hockey, wrestling, shooting, and boxing.
  • Track and Field Events
    • Track and field is a sport comprising various competitive athletic contests based on running, jumping, and throwing.
    • The sport is categorized under the umbrella of athletics, which also includes road running, cross country running, and racewalking.
    • Track and field events are typically held on a running track and a grass field within a stadium.
    • Some of the standard events in track and field include sprints, middle-distance and long-distance races, hurdles, relays, long jump, high jump, pole vault, shot put, discus throw, javelin throw, and hammer throw.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first event in a triathlon?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the first event in a triathlon?
questions.solution: Swimming is the first discipline in a triathlon. A standard triathlon involves three sequential endurance events: swimming, cycling, and running. questions.solution: The 2023 ICC Men's ODI Cricket World Cup was the 13th edition of the tournament. It was hosted solely by India for the first time, having previously co-hosted in 1987, 1996, and 2011. The event featured 10 teams competing in a round-robin format, followed by knockouts.

questions.question: Which track and field event has a water jump?
questions.questionHtml: Which track and field event has a water jump?
questions.solution: Steeplechase is a track and field event involving running and hurdling over obstacles, including 28 hurdles and 7 water jumps in a 3000-meter race. The water jump is a pit filled with water, positioned after a hurdle, measuring 3.66 meters long and 70 cm deep at its base.

questions.question: Which of the following sports was included as a discipline in the 11 th Asian Games Beijing 1990?

questions.solution: Kabaddi was included as a discipline in the 11th Asian Games held in Beijing in 1990, marking its debut internationally. India dominated Kabaddi, winning multiple golds. questions.question: What is the standard width of the field in an international hockey match?
questions.questionHtml: What is the standard width of the field in an international hockey match?
questions.solution: The standard width of the field in an international hockey match is 55 meters as per FIH regulations. The field is rectangular (91.4m x 55m), divided into halves with key markings, and played on synthetic turf. Goals are centrally placed with dimensions of 3.66m width and 2.14m height.
